questions.answers: One row per concept with either state recorded.
questions.description: Concepts with an architecture state (baseline, target, transitional) or an approval state (proposed, approved).
questions.does_not_prove: That a concept without a state is current. An unstated state is unknown.
questions.label: What is baseline, target or still awaiting approval?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per path: its length, the concept it starts from, the concept between, and the relationship types.
questions.description: Concepts from which a path of one or two relationships ends at the element, with the relationship types along the way.
questions.does_not_prove: Impact. Reachability is not dependency: an assignment followed by an association does not make the last concept depend on the first. Read the types, and use a language's impact question where there is one.
questions.label: What reaches this element within two hops?

parameters.description: The element the question is about. A modelling tool binds the selected element.
parameters.name: focus

questions.answers: One row per element in a collision, with how many elements share the name.
questions.description: Elements whose name, compared without regard to case, another element of the same most specific type also has, in any loaded model.
questions.does_not_prove: That they are the same thing. A shared name makes two elements candidates for a person to compare, never a merge.
questions.label: Which elements share a name with another of the same type?

parameters.description: The model whose elements are reported. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per property and value of the concept.
questions.description: Every statement about one concept, with the name of each value that has one.
questions.does_not_prove: That an unrecorded property is false. The model records what was said, nothing about what was not.
questions.label: What is recorded about this element?

parameters.description: The concept the question is about. A modelling tool binds the selected element.
parameters.name: focus

questions.answers: One row per element, with its most specific type.
questions.description: The elements of one type (of every type when none is given), with their names and definitions.
questions.does_not_prove: That no other element plays the part: an element of a specialisation is listed only where it is also typed with the type asked for.
questions.label: Which elements are of this type?

parameters.description: An element type, such as an application component.
parameters.name: concept type

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per element without a definition.
questions.description: Elements, of one type or of any, with no skos:definition.
questions.does_not_prove: That the element is unclear to its readers. A self-explanatory name may need no definition.
questions.label: Which elements have no definition?

parameters.description: An element type, such as an application component.
parameters.name: concept type

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per type: its kind (element, relationship, view) and how many of the model's concepts are of it.
questions.description: The model's elements, relationships and views, counted by type.
questions.does_not_prove: That the model is complete. The counts describe what was modelled, not what exists in the enterprise.
questions.label: What does the model contain?

parameters.description: The model to count. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per relationship: its direction seen from the element, its type and the concept at its other end.
questions.description: Every relationship that starts or ends at the element, read from the qualified relationships.
questions.does_not_prove: A runtime dependency. A modelled relationship is a statement someone made, not an observed call.
questions.label: What is this element directly related to?

parameters.description: The element the question is about. A modelling tool binds the selected element.
parameters.name: focus

questions.answers: One row per unconnected element.
questions.description: Elements that are neither the source nor the target of any relationship.
questions.does_not_prove: That the element is unused or safe to delete. It may be context drawn on a diagram, or its relationships may be in a model that is not loaded.
questions.label: Which elements take part in no relationship?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per relationship in error, with what is wrong.
questions.description:
Qualified relationships whose type has an unqualified form (arch:unqualifiedForm) but whose
rdf:reifies triple term is missing or names other ends, or whose direct triple is not asserted. Needs RDF 1.2
triple terms.
questions.does_not_prove: That a query over the direct triples is wrong everywhere: it misses or misreports exactly these relationships.
questions.label: Which relationships are out of step with their direct triple?

questions.answers: One row per view, with the viewpoint it names.
questions.description:
Views whose arch:viewConformsToViewpoint names a resource nothing loaded defines — a
misspelt or outdated viewpoint IRI, or a metamodel that is not loaded. Their conformance cannot be judged.
questions.does_not_prove: That the viewpoint does not exist: it may be defined in a metamodel that is not loaded.
questions.label: Which views follow a viewpoint the loaded metamodels do not define?

questions.answers: One row per element without arch:inView.
questions.description: Elements of the model that no diagram, catalogue or matrix presents.
questions.does_not_prove: That the element is irrelevant. Much of a model is only ever queried; this matters where a deliverable is read as complete.
questions.label: Which elements appear in no view?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per presented concept, with its most specific type.
questions.description: The elements and relationships a view presents.
questions.does_not_prove: Layout or grouping: nesting on a diagram is geometry, not a relationship.
questions.label: What does this view present?

parameters.description: A view. A modelling tool binds the open view.
parameters.name: view

questions.answers: One row per view presenting the element.
questions.description: The views that present the element, with their viewpoints.
questions.does_not_prove: That a view not listed leaves it out on purpose: a view drawn without arch:inView may still place it.
questions.label: Which views show this element?

parameters.description: The element the question is about. A modelling tool binds the selected element.
parameters.name: focus

questions.answers: One row per element out of place: the view, its viewpoint, the element and its type.
questions.description:
Elements presented in a view whose viewpoint states the concepts it admits
(arch:includesConcept), and whose type is neither one of them nor a specialisation of one. Views whose
viewpoint the loaded metamodels do not define are the subject of "Which views follow a viewpoint the loaded
metamodels do not define?".
questions.does_not_prove: That the view is wrong. A viewpoint is a convention; the finding is that the view departs from it, which may be deliberate.
questions.label: Which elements does their view's viewpoint not admit?

parameters.description: A view to check; every view when none is given. A modelling tool binds the open view.
parameters.name: view

questions.answers: One row per element: name, type, definition and a "relationship → target" summary of what it points to.
questions.description:
Elements whose type the viewpoint admits — a type it names or a specialisation of
one — each with its outgoing relationships summarised. The viewpoint is the one statement of what a view or a
deliverable section covers.
questions.does_not_prove: That the elements belong in one diagram. A viewpoint says what may appear, not what should be drawn together.
questions.label: What in the model belongs in a view of this viewpoint?

parameters.description: A viewpoint. A modelling tool binds the open view's viewpoint; a deliverable, the section's.
parameters.name: viewpoint

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per dependency: the provider, how it provides, the relationship or service between, and the consumer.
questions.description: Application components that serve, flow to or trigger one another, directly or through an application service one realises — itself or through the function assigned to it — and the other is served by.
questions.does_not_prove: Runtime coupling or data volume. A modelled flow says that information moves, not how much or how often.
questions.label: Which applications depend on which?

questions.answers: One row per application component with no technology under it.
questions.description: Application components that no element of the technology layer serves or realises, directly or by realising a service that serves them. Equipment and facilities are nodes, so they count as technology.
questions.does_not_prove: That it runs nowhere. Where it is hosted may be outside the model, or recorded only in a deployment model that is not loaded.
questions.label: Which application components run on no technology?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per capability and what realises it; a capability nothing realises appears once, with nothing beside it.
questions.description: Capabilities with the behaviour, active structure or resources that realise them.
questions.does_not_prove: Maturity. That a capability is realised says it is delivered somehow, not how well.
questions.label: What realises each capability?

questions.answers: One row per access: what accesses, the kind of access, and the object accessed.
questions.description: Access relationships by kind: ArchiMate 3.2 types the kind (am:ReadAccess, am:WriteAccess, am:ReadWriteAccess, and am:Access when it is not stated).
questions.does_not_prove: Ownership of the data. Write access is not mastery; arch:masterDataSource says where that is recorded.
questions.label: Who reads and writes which information?

questions.answers: One row per object, with how many elements read it.
questions.description: Data objects, business objects (contracts too) and artifacts that something reads and nothing writes. Access of an unstated kind (am:Access) counts as a possible write.
questions.does_not_prove: That the data has no source. It may be written by a system outside the model; that boundary is what the finding asks to discuss.
questions.label: Which information is read but never written?

questions.answers: One row per layer, with the number of elements in it.
questions.description: Elements counted by ArchiMate 3.2 layer, read from the layer classes their types specialise, so specialisations count where they belong.
questions.does_not_prove: Balance. Equipment and facilities are nodes as well as physical, so they count in both the technology and the physical layer; location, grouping and junctions belong to no layer and are not counted.
questions.label: How is the model spread over the ArchiMate layers?

parameters.description: The model to count. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per element that depends on the element, directly or through others.
questions.description: Everything that depends on the element, transitively, by ArchiMate's dependency relationships: what it serves, realises or is assigned to, and what accesses it.
questions.does_not_prove: That each is broken by the change. Dynamic relationships (flow, triggering) and structure (composition, aggregation) are not followed, and a dependency may tolerate the change.
questions.label: What is affected if this element changes?

parameters.description: The element that changes. A modelling tool binds the selected element; a deliverable, the element it is produced for.
parameters.name: focus

questions.answers: One row per source layer, relationship type and target layer, with the number of relationships.
questions.description: Relationships whose ends are in different ArchiMate 3.2 layers, counted by pair of layers and relationship type. The layers are read from the layer classes, not from type names.
questions.does_not_prove: Coupling. A relationship to an element of no layer (location, grouping, junction) is not counted, and one between equipment and a node crosses from the physical to the technology layer though both are nodes.
questions.label: Which relationships cross layers, and of which kind?

questions.answers: One row per element added or removed.
questions.description: Elements a later plateau aggregates or is composed of that an earlier one is not (added), and the reverse (removed).
questions.does_not_prove: The migration path. The difference is the gap; the work packages that close it are another question.
questions.label: What changes between these two plateaus?

parameters.description: The earlier plateau, such as the baseline.
parameters.name: from

parameters.description: The later plateau, such as the target.
parameters.name: to

questions.answers: One row per relationship between a principle and another element.
questions.description: Principles with the elements they relate to in either direction: the drivers and goals behind them, the requirements that realise them.
questions.does_not_prove: Compliance. A requirement realising a principle states an intent, not that designs follow it.
questions.label: What motivates each principle, and what does it constrain?

questions.answers: One row per principle no requirement realises.
questions.description: Principles that no requirement or constraint realises.
questions.does_not_prove: That the principle is ignored. It may be applied by review rather than through stated requirements.
questions.label: Which principles has no requirement made concrete?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per traced link: the requirement, the direction, the predicate and the element at the other end.
questions.description: Requirements and constraints with what realises them, below, and the goals, outcomes and principles they realise or influence, above, as a list of links.
questions.does_not_prove: Verification. A realisation relationship is a design claim; it does not show the requirement is met.
questions.label: How does each requirement trace to goals and to the elements that realise it?

questions.answers: One row per assignment, with both ends and their types.
questions.description: Assignment relationships: which actor, role, collaboration, component or node performs which behaviour or plays which role.
questions.does_not_prove: Accountability in the RACI sense. An ArchiMate assignment states who performs, not who answers for the outcome.
questions.label: Who is responsible for what?

questions.answers: One row per relationship between a stakeholder and a motivation element.
questions.description: Stakeholders and the motivation elements (drivers, assessments, goals, outcomes, principles, requirements, constraints, values, meanings) they are related to, in either direction.
questions.does_not_prove: Priority. That a stakeholder is associated with a goal does not rank it among their concerns.
questions.label: What do stakeholders care about?

questions.answers: One row per process or function without a performer, with the kind asked about.
questions.description: Business, application and technology processes and functions that no active structure element is assigned to.
questions.does_not_prove: That nobody performs it. The performer may be assigned to an enclosing process, or the model may stop above that level of detail.
questions.label: Which processes and functions has nobody been assigned to?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per capability with no realisation anywhere beneath it.
questions.description: Capabilities realised neither directly nor through any capability they are composed of or aggregate.
questions.does_not_prove: That the enterprise lacks the capability; only that the model does not say what delivers it.
questions.label: Which capabilities does nothing realise?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.answers: One row per requirement or constraint without a realising design element.
questions.description: Requirements and constraints that no element outside the motivation elements realises: realisation by another motivation element does not count.
questions.does_not_prove: That the requirement is unmet; only that the model does not show what meets it.
questions.label: Which requirements does no architecture element realise?

parameters.description: The model to look in. A modelling tool binds the open model; a deliverable, the model it is produced from.
parameters.name: model

questions.description:
What belongs in a view of an ArchiMate 4.0 viewpoint. ArchiMate 4.0 places process,
function, service, event and role in a common domain, and viewpoints such as the Technology Viewpoint admit them;
listed whenever their type is admitted, every business process would belong in a technology view. An element of the
common domain therefore belongs when a relationship connects it, in either direction, to an element of a
domain-specific type the same viewpoint admits; every other element belongs when the viewpoint admits its type.
questions.does_not_prove: That an element of the common domain left out is irrelevant to the viewpoint; only that nothing of a domain-specific type the viewpoint admits is related to it.
questions.label: What in the model belongs in a view of this ArchiMate viewpoint?
